cardiac-tamponade-fixtures.ts binds seed 7268 and content 0.1.0 to expert, picture-before-the-patient error, recovery, and no-action paths. The penetrating central-chest trauma with tachycardia, a narrowing pulse pressure, cool skin, inattention and falling end-tidal carbon dioxide alongside preserved bilateral air entry; the single fixed focused-ultrasound statement of pericardial fluid with right-sided chamber collapse; and the post-intent monitor that remains compatible with unresolved obstructive shock are authored constants. The obstructive burden itself comes from the shared engine event declared at arrival and is not relieved by any recorded action: no procedure, no treatment response, no technical success and no outcome is simulated. tests/integration/emergency-cardiac-tamponade-runs.test.ts replays every path frame-for-frame across all three guidance levels and both practice regions.

The progression lives in the engine's gates across four recorded steps in one strict chain: the whole-patient review is gated ahead of the focused finding, the finding ahead of the definitive-control intent, and the reassessment behind the intent plus one further engine tick. Unusually, the modelled physiology does not progress in the learner's favour at any point — the obstructive burden declared at arrival is still running when the branch ends, and the engine records that in the reassessment event rather than leaving it to be inferred. Every refusal is exercised by a reference transcript.

Four recorded decisions against four declared objectives: review the mechanism together with the perfusion findings and the preserved bilateral air entry that separates this from a tension pneumothorax; review one fixed focused-ultrasound statement, second rather than first; record immediate trauma, surgical and resuscitation-team mobilisation for definitive control; and reassess perfusion after a further tick without inferring that anything was relieved. The lesson acquires and interprets no image, teaches no view, offers no pericardiocentesis or thoracotomy and no technique, transports nobody, delivers no fluid or vasopressor as a bounded control, adjudicates no differential, and predicts no outcome. The single escalation control is explicitly an intent that mobilises care rather than an act that relieves tamponade.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The branch ends at a recorded reassessment that finds the canonical monitor still compatible with unresolved obstructive shock. Later actions cannot restart an ended branch. This is the deliberate inversion of the usual ending: the engine reports physiologyResolved false and treatmentDelivered false on the event, and the lesson says in the learner-visible prose that the right action was recorded and the physiology is unchanged. The ending hands over an unresolved patient and an urgent need for live definitive care rather than a claim of improvement.

Four observed-state prompts at version 0.1.0 read the learner's own recorded steps. The reflex the lesson works against is the one every other lesson quietly rewards — that recording the right action is what makes the patient better. The context beat makes the preserved bilateral air entry do real work, since tension pneumothorax is the pair this pattern gets sorted into, and reads the narrowing pulse pressure and the falling end-tidal carbon dioxide as two ways of being told about stroke volume. The focused-finding beat says why it comes second: an effusion is only tamponade when the circulation says it is, and reading the screen before the patient is how a finding gets promoted into a diagnosis it has not earned. The escalation beat says why there is no procedure on the screen — in penetrating traumatic tamponade the pericardial clot is generally not something a needle empties, so the definitive answer is an operation and the only thing available to compress is the interval before it starts. The reassessment beat tells the learner to expect nothing better and says why that is the point of looking. Worked example 0.1.0 drives the ordinary controls through the real engine to a reassessment that finds unresolved shock, and asks the tutor for its narration rather than storing a copy. A test asserts that no beat anywhere performs the procedure, claims the obstruction is relieved, or reports an improving monitor. tests/unit/emergency-cardiac-tamponade-worked-example.test.ts verifies every beat and every refusal against the real engine, and tests/ui/emergency-cardiac-tamponade.test.tsx verifies the tray, silence when unassisted, stable controls while watching, and version binding alongside the pre-existing tests/ui/cardiac-tamponade.test.tsx.

src/modules/anesthesia/ui/Debrief.tsx maps the declared objectives to accepted engine events; the no-action path meets none and the expert path meets all four. The counterfactual is the one that reads the screen before the patient: the common-error path reaches for the fixed focused-ultrasound statement first and is refused, then records the control intent and is refused again, because a finding nobody has put in context cannot authorise an escalation. The recovery path reaches for the control intent before the finding that supports it and is refused, reaches for the reassessment on the same tick as the accepted intent and is refused again, and still completes from the same positions.

emergency-anaphylaxis-fixtures.ts binds seed 4174 and content 0.1.0 to expert, adjuncts-before-the-drug error, recovery, and no-action paths. The thirty-four-year-old man of 75 kg with mild asthma and a reported peanut allergy, presenting minutes after a community food exposure with lip and tongue swelling, widespread wheeze, hypoxaemia, hypotension and impaired perfusion and with skin findings deliberately absent; the fixed adult 500-microgram intramuscular anterolateral-thigh epinephrine action; the high-flow non-rebreather oxygen record; and the fixed 1,500 mL isotonic crystalloid bolus are authored constants. No absorption, pharmacokinetic, airway-swelling or treatment-response model is claimed beyond the shared anaphylaxis event present on arrival, no repeat dose is offered, and no outcome follows from any choice. tests/integration/emergency-anaphylaxis-runs.test.ts replays every path frame-for-frame across all three guidance levels and both practice regions.

The progression lives in the engine's gates across six recorded steps, and the fourth gate carries the lesson: the intramuscular epinephrine is gated ahead of both supportive adjuncts, so oxygen and a fluid bolus cannot be recorded first. The pattern review is gated ahead of everything, positioning and help ahead of the drug, the two adjuncts are gated against each other not at all, and the reassessment sits behind both plus one further engine tick. Every one of those refusals is exercised by a reference transcript.

Six recorded decisions against four declared objectives: review the fixed airway, breathing, circulation and exposure pattern including the deliberately absent skin findings; record recumbent positioning, trigger removal, monitoring and emergency help; record the fixed adult 500-microgram intramuscular epinephrine action; record high-flow oxygen; begin the fixed 1,500 mL crystalloid bolus; and reassess airway, breathing, circulation, mental status and the monitor after a further tick. The two adjuncts are unordered because neither is a prerequisite for the other. The lesson examines nobody, draws up and injects nothing, offers no intravenous bolus of epinephrine and no dose calculator, positions no one physically, verifies no trigger, manages no airway, offers no repeat dose, determines no disposition or observation period, and predicts no outcome.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The branch ends at a recorded reassessment of airway, breathing, circulation, mental status and the canonical monitor response. Later actions cannot restart an ended branch. The monitor improvement is authored rather than modelled and the lesson says so where a learner will read it, alongside the three things the vignette deliberately withholds: a repeat dose, a biphasic reaction, and an airway that keeps swelling. The ending hands over a prompt to keep looking rather than a claim that the response worked.

Seven observed-state prompts at version 0.1.0 read the learner's own recorded steps. The reflex the lesson works against is preparation: oxygen and vascular access feel like what you do before giving a drug, and in anaphylaxis they are the two things most likely to be underway while the one intervention that changes the outcome has not happened yet — which is why the engine gates the drug ahead of both, and why the refusal is treated as the teaching rather than as an obstacle. The pattern beat makes the absent skin findings the point, and notes that they are missing more often in the severe presentations, which is the wrong way round for a rule that says wait for hives. The positioning beat says why standing a hypotensive anaphylaxis patient up is itself dangerous, and therefore why positioning is a gated treatment step rather than tidying. The epinephrine beat says why the anterolateral thigh and why not intravenously. Because the two adjuncts are unordered, the claim about the fluid — that a large share of the circulating volume has moved into the tissues, so the bolus replaces something that has genuinely gone — lives in the beat for the state where neither has been recorded, the only such beat every path passes through, together with the reminder that neither adjunct substitutes for a second dose. The reassessment beat says the honest answer after a first dose is often "not yet, give it again", and that the authored improvement is a prompt to keep looking. Worked example 0.1.0 drives the ordinary controls through the real engine and asks the tutor for its narration rather than storing a copy. A test asserts that no beat anywhere gives the drug intravenously, names a technique, sits the patient up, or claims the reaction is over. tests/unit/emergency-anaphylaxis-worked-example.test.ts verifies every beat and every refusal against the real engine, and tests/ui/emergency-anaphylaxis-tutor.test.tsx verifies the tray, silence when unassisted, stable controls while watching, and version binding alongside the pre-existing tests/ui/emergency-anaphylaxis.test.tsx.

src/modules/anesthesia/ui/Debrief.tsx maps the declared objectives to accepted engine events; the no-action path meets none and the expert path meets all four. The counterfactual is the one that treats the adjuncts as preparation: the common-error path reviews the pattern, records positioning and help, and then reaches for oxygen and the fluid bolus before the intramuscular epinephrine. Both are refused, and the two objectives downstream of the drug stay unmet. The recovery path reaches for the drug before positioning and help are recorded and is refused, reaches for the reassessment on the same tick as the second adjunct and is refused again, and still completes from the same positions.

adult-asthma-fixtures.ts binds seed 3412 and content 0.1.0 to expert, deferred-corticosteroid error, recovery, and no-action paths. The forty-one-year-old woman of 68 kg with known asthma and one prior admission, speaking single words with accessory-muscle use, respiratory rate 34/min, SpO2 91% on room air and a peak expiratory flow of 32% predicted; the absent urticaria, angioedema, focal air-entry loss, fever and oedema that the authored review records; the fixed six-puff salbutamol and four-puff ipratropium pressurised-inhaler-and-spacer bundle; the fixed adult oxygen target band of 92 to 95%; and the authored repeat peak flow of 55% predicted are authored constants. No airway-obstruction, bronchodilator, corticosteroid or treatment-response model is claimed beyond the shared obstruction event present on arrival, and no outcome follows from any choice. tests/integration/emergency-adult-asthma-runs.test.ts replays every path frame-for-frame across all three guidance levels and both practice regions.

The progression lives in the engine's gates across five recorded steps, and the shape of those gates is the lesson: the severity and mimic review is gated ahead of all treatment, the three initial treatments are gated against nothing at all and may be recorded in any order, and the reassessment is gated behind all three plus one further engine tick. Both the order refusal and the too-early reassessment refusal are exercised by a reference transcript.

Five recorded decisions against four declared objectives: review the authored severity findings, the two that carry a number and the immediate alternative causes the review excludes; record controlled oxygen against a target band rather than a direction of travel; give the fixed conservative inhaled bronchodilator bundle by pressurised inhaler and spacer; record systemic-corticosteroid intent within the first hour; and reassess symptoms, signs, oxygenation, waveform and peak flow after a further tick. The three treatments are unordered because none is a prerequisite for the others. The lesson examines nobody, performs no spirometry, blood gas or imaging, prepares and delivers no drug, teaches no inhaler technique, sets no device, individualises no dose, repeats no cycle, determines no disposition, writes no prescription, and predicts no outcome.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The branch ends at a recorded reassessment against an authored repeat peak flow of 55% predicted. Later actions cannot restart an ended branch. That number is an authored constant rather than a modelled response, and the lesson says so where a learner will read it, so the ending hands over a prompt to look again rather than a claim that the treatment worked or a decision about disposition.

Six observed-state prompts at version 0.1.0 read the learner's own recorded steps. The reflex the lesson works against is the verdict: three initial treatments are open at once and none waits on another, but they act on three different clocks, and the slowest of the three is the one whose entire advantage is being given early — so it is the one held back until the fast treatment has been judged, which is the only deferral here that cannot be recovered in the same visit. Because the three lanes are unordered, that claim lives in the beat for the state where none of them has been recorded, the only such beat every path passes through. The severity beat names speech and peak flow as the two findings that grade it and says a quiet chest here would be worse rather than better. The oxygen beat reads the 92 to 95% band as a target that can be missed in both directions rather than a direction of travel. The bronchodilator beat says why a spacer is not the budget option at this severity and why ipratropium is in a severe-exacerbation bundle specifically. The reassessment beat says why a second treatment cycle should follow a second look rather than a clock, why the reassessment is gated behind a further tick, and that the numbers that come back are authored rather than modelled. Worked example 0.1.0 drives the ordinary controls through the real engine, deliberately records the hours-away drug before the minutes-away one to make the absence of a rank visible, and asks the tutor for its narration rather than storing a copy. A test asserts that no beat anywhere teaches inhaler technique, names an individualised dose, opens the oxygen without a ceiling, or claims the treatment worked. tests/unit/emergency-adult-asthma-worked-example.test.ts verifies every beat and every refusal against the real engine, and tests/ui/emergency-adult-asthma.test.tsx verifies the tray, silence when unassisted, stable controls while watching, and version binding.

src/modules/anesthesia/ui/Debrief.tsx maps the declared objectives to accepted engine events; the no-action path meets none and the expert path meets all four. The counterfactual is the one that saves the slow drug for after the verdict: the common-error path reviews severity, records oxygen and the inhaled bundle, and then reaches for the reassessment intending to decide about corticosteroid once the nebulised treatment has been judged. It is refused, and the objective that pairs the two treatment intents stays unmet. The recovery path reaches for the inhaled bundle before the severity review and is refused, reaches for the reassessment on the same tick as the last of the three treatments and is refused again, and still completes from the same positions.

acute-pulmonary-edema-fixtures.ts binds seed 5150 and content 0.1.0 to expert, diuretic-alone error, recovery, and no-action paths. The seventy-two-year-old woman of 74 kg with abrupt dyspnoea and orthopnoea, short-phrase speech, respiratory rate 32/min, SpO2 90%, blood pressure 188/112 mmHg, diffuse crackles and a raised jugular venous pressure; the authored ECG showing sinus tachycardia without ST elevation, the radiograph showing a bilateral perihilar interstitial-alveolar pattern and the focused ultrasound showing diffuse B-lines with preserved left ventricular contraction; the bounded FiO2 0.40 and PEEP 8 cmH2O teaching display; and the post-treatment monitor at RR 22/min, SpO2 96% and 146/86 mmHg are authored constants. No edema, diuresis, vasodilator, ventilation or treatment-response model is claimed, and no outcome follows from any choice. tests/integration/emergency-acute-pulmonary-edema-runs.test.ts replays every path frame-for-frame across all three guidance levels and both practice regions.

The shared audit records this requirement as missing because the timeline is a single narrative boundary with no non-narrative state event. Both the order refusal and the too-early reassessment refusal are exercised by a reference transcript.

Five recorded decisions against four declared objectives: review the respiratory, congestion, pressure and perfusion findings together with the authored ECG, radiograph and ultrasound, the immediate mimics they exclude and the precipitants they do not; record early noninvasive positive pressure with titrated oxygen; record an intravenous loop-diuretic intent for the authored congestion; record an intravenous vasodilator intent on a systolic pressure safely above 110 mmHg; and reassess breathing, oxygenation, pressure and perfusion after a further tick. The three treatments are unordered because none is a prerequisite for the others. The lesson examines nobody, acquires and interprets no test or image, sets up no interface, prepares and delivers no drug, titrates nothing, treats no precipitant, determines no disposition, and predicts no outcome.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The branch ends at a recorded reassessment against an authored monitor: RR 22/min, SpO2 96%, blood pressure 146/86 mmHg. Later actions cannot restart an ended branch. Those numbers are authored constants rather than a modelled response, and the lesson says so where a learner will read it, so the ending hands over a prompt to look again rather than a claim that the treatment worked.

Six observed-state prompts at version 0.1.0 read the learner's own recorded steps. The reflex the lesson works against is rank: three initial treatments are open at once and none waits on the others, but one of the three is the word most people have filed under "pulmonary edema" and it is the slowest of the three at what the next few minutes need. Because the three lanes are unordered, the claim the lesson turns on lives in the beat for the state where none of them has been recorded, which is the only such beat every path passes through — preserved contraction and a systolic of 188 point at redistribution rather than an accumulation of litres, so positive pressure is the fastest lever and recording the diuretic does not buy the other two. The pressure beat names the qualifying systolic and reads afterload reduction as the same problem seen from the other end. The diuretic beat is honest about when natriuresis starts to matter. The reassessment beat says why it is gated behind a further tick, and that the numbers that come back are authored rather than modelled. Worked example 0.1.0 drives the ordinary controls through the real engine, takes the fastest treatment first and the most familiar last to make the absence of a rank visible, and asks the tutor for its narration rather than storing a copy. A test asserts that no beat anywhere sets up the interface, names a dose, titrates a drug, or claims the treatment worked. tests/unit/emergency-acute-pulmonary-edema-worked-example.test.ts verifies every beat and every refusal against the real engine, and tests/ui/emergency-acute-pulmonary-edema.test.tsx verifies the tray, silence when unassisted, stable controls while watching, and version binding.

The counterfactual is the one that ranks the three treatments: the common-error path reviews the pattern, records the loop-diuretic intent alone because that is the word filed under pulmonary edema, and then reaches for the reassessment with positive pressure and the vasodilator never recorded. It is refused, and the two objectives that turn on them stay unmet. The recovery path reaches for support before the pattern review and is refused, reaches for the reassessment on the same tick as the last of the three treatments and is refused again, and still completes from the same positions.

acute-ischemic-stroke-fixtures.ts binds seed 6842 and content 0.1.0 to expert, transfer-waiting-on-the-drug error, recovery, and no-action paths. The sixty-eight-year-old woman of 80 kg with witnessed sudden aphasia and right facial and arm weakness, last known well 70 minutes ago, glucose 112 mg/dL, BP 168/94 mmHg, a protected airway and spontaneous breathing; the authored noncontrast CT showing no intracranial haemorrhage and CTA showing a left M1 large-vessel occlusion with no authored contraindication; the local-protocol tenecteplase 20 mg intent from a 0.25 mg/kg teaching calculation capped at 25 mg; and the fixed surveillance handoff at BP 168/94 mmHg with no overt bleeding are authored constants. No stroke, imaging, pharmacologic or reperfusion model is claimed, no treatment response is produced, and no outcome follows from any choice. tests/integration/emergency-acute-ischemic-stroke-runs.test.ts replays every path frame-for-frame across all three guidance levels and both practice regions.

The shared audit records this requirement as missing because the timeline is two narratives with no non-narrative state event. The progression lives in the engine's five order refusals across six recorded steps, and the fifth carries the lesson: the thrombectomy transfer is its own gated action, taken explicitly without waiting for a thrombolysis response, so the two reperfusion pathways cannot collapse into a sequence. The imaging review is gated ahead of any reperfusion intent, and the handoff behind the transfer. Every refusal is exercised by a reference transcript.

Six recorded decisions against five declared objectives: review the disabling deficit, witnessed last-known-well time, glucose, pressure, airway and breathing without examining or scoring severity; activate the stroke system, monitoring, vascular access, laboratory workflow and parallel noncontrast CT plus CTA; review the authored CT, CTA, pressure and contraindication findings without interpreting images or adjudicating real eligibility; record a local-protocol tenecteplase 20 mg intent within 4.5 hours from a 0.25 mg/kg teaching calculation capped at 25 mg; activate the endovascular pathway and immediate thrombectomy-capable-centre transfer for the authored left M1 occlusion without waiting for thrombolysis response; and record fixed surveillance and a handoff carrying the last-known-well, activation, imaging, thrombolysis-intent and transfer clocks. The lesson examines nobody, scores no severity, acquires and interprets no image, prepares and delivers no drug, transfers nobody, performs no procedure, diagnoses nothing, determines no disposition, and predicts no outcome.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The branch ends at a recorded surveillance and handoff: airway still protected, breathing spontaneous, BP 168/94 mmHg and no overt bleeding authored. Later actions cannot restart an ended branch. Deficits are deliberately not re-scored and no treatment response is claimed, so the ending hands over a set of clocks rather than a judgement about whether anything worked.

Six observed-state prompts at version 0.1.0 read the learner's own recorded steps — one per recorded step. The reflex the lesson works against is sequence: thrombolysis reads like the treatment and thrombectomy like the fallback, so the transfer waits on a response that takes longer to declare itself than the transfer takes to arrange, and a clot in an M1 is often too big for a drug to clear. The presentation beat makes "witnessed" the reason the clock is a fact rather than an estimate and names the glucose as the mimic not to miss on the way to a reperfusion pathway. The activation beat argues for CT and CTA as one trip rather than two and says how this race is lost — serially, with each sensible step waiting for the one before it. The imaging beat treats the noncontrast CT as a permission rather than a diagnosis, since an early ischaemic stroke often looks normal on it, and names the CTA finding as what makes this a two-pathway problem. The thrombolysis beat points at the 25 mg cap as where weight-based dosing stops being weight-based. The handoff beat explains why the deficits are deliberately not re-scored, and why a set of times is a more useful handover than a label. Worked example 0.1.0 drives the ordinary controls through the real engine to the handoff and asks the tutor for its narration rather than storing a copy. A test asserts that no beat anywhere pushes the drug, reads the images itself, lowers the blood pressure, or claims a reperfusion result. tests/unit/emergency-acute-ischemic-stroke-worked-example.test.ts verifies every beat and every refusal against the real engine, and tests/ui/emergency-acute-ischemic-stroke.test.tsx verifies the tray, silence when unassisted, stable controls while watching, and version binding.

src/modules/anesthesia/ui/Debrief.tsx maps the declared objectives to accepted engine events; the no-action path meets none and the expert path meets all five. The counterfactual is the one that turns two parallel pathways into a queue: the common-error path records the presentation, activation, imaging and thrombolysis intent and then reaches for the handoff with the transfer still outstanding, and is refused because the engine gates the handoff behind the transfer. The recovery path reaches for activation before the presentation has been reviewed and is refused, reaches for the thrombolysis intent before the imaging that permits it and is refused again, and still completes from the same positions.

acute-aortic-syndrome-fixtures.ts binds seed 7481 and content 0.1.0 to expert, escalate-before-the-repeat-exam error, recovery, and no-action paths. The fifty-eight-year-old hypertensive man with abrupt severe chest pain maximal at onset 18 minutes ago and now interscapular, at HR 104/min and SpO2 96% on room air with initial arm pressures of 198/106 and 194/104 mmHg, symmetric pulses, perfusion and neurology and a nondiagnostic ECG; the authored six-minute evolution to left-arm 202/108 against right-arm 166/92 mmHg, a 36 mmHg difference, a newly weak right radial, a cool left foot with diminished pedal pulse and delayed refill, new mild left-arm drift with clear speech and glucose 112 mg/dL; the recorded targets of HR 60-80/min and systolic below 120 mmHg only where perfusion is preserved; and the pre-imaging repeat at HR 82/min with left-arm 156/88 and right-arm 132/78 mmHg are authored constants. No aortic, haemodynamic or imaging model is claimed, the scan never results, and no outcome follows from any choice. tests/integration/acute-aortic-syndrome-runs.test.ts replays every path frame-for-frame across all three guidance levels and both practice regions.

The shared audit records this requirement as missing because the timeline is two narratives with no non-narrative state event. The progression lives in the engine's five order refusals across six recorded steps, and the second step carries the lesson: the first examination is authored symmetric, and the engine makes repeating it a recorded action gated ahead of every pathway decision, so a suspicion becomes three disagreeing territories before anything is escalated or given. The anti-impulse intent is in turn gated ahead of the imaging priority, and the closing repeat behind both. Every refusal is exercised by a reference transcript.

Six recorded decisions against five declared objectives: synthesize the incomplete initial pain, ECG, bilateral pressure, pulse, perfusion and neurologic pattern while keeping acute coronary and other dangerous chest-pain causes plausible and recording no default antithrombotic pathway; repeat bilateral pressures, pulses, limb perfusion and neurologic findings to reveal the authored evolving asymmetry without claiming a diagnosis; escalate to multidisciplinary aortic and critical-care teams while explicitly pausing routine coronary anticoagulation or thrombolysis and isolated stroke thrombolysis pending urgent evaluation; record ICU-level monitoring, arterial-line intent, titrated analgesia and local-protocol intravenous rate control before any vasodilator, with HR 60-80/min and systolic below 120 mmHg qualified by preserved end-organ perfusion; prioritize urgent definitive CT of the aorta and branch vessels while the patient is transportable, with TEE or MRI as a context-dependent alternative and the result explicitly unavailable; and repeat the serial assessment and hand off the uncertainty. The lesson examines nobody, gives no drug and selects no dose, places no line, acquires and interprets no image, consults, transfers and operates on nobody, makes no diagnosis, determines no disposition, and predicts no outcome.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The branch ends at a recorded serial reassessment and handoff — pain still present, HR 82/min, left-arm 156/88 and right-arm 132/78 mmHg, persistent weak right radial and left pedal pulses, a still-cool left foot and unchanged mild left-arm drift with clear speech — with the scan explicitly not available. Later actions cannot restart an ended branch. The ending hands over the times, trends, recorded intents, competing diagnoses, malperfusion concern and the missing result rather than a label, and no diagnosis, image result, procedure, transfer, disposition or outcome is simulated.

Six observed-state prompts at version 0.1.0 read the learner's own recorded steps — one per recorded step. The reflex the lesson works against is the default pathway: a hypertensive man with crushing chest pain and a nondiagnostic ECG is an acute coronary syndrome until proven otherwise, and the treatment for that is the drug you would least like to have given a dissecting aorta. The initial beat picks out "maximal at onset" as the word that separates this from most cardiac pain, which builds, and makes the step's value what it declines to start. The evolution beat says a symmetric examination is a fact about a moment rather than a promise, reads an arm, a leg and a brain as one process at a branch point rather than three diagnoses, and notes the glucose of 112 removes the cheapest explanation for the drift. The escalation beat names both paused pathways and distinguishes pausing from ruling out. The anti-impulse beat explains why the order is the content — a vasodilator at a heart rate of 104 increases the force of each ejection, which is the thing tearing the aorta — and puts a ceiling on chasing the targets, because a lower pressure that starves a cool foot or a drifting arm is not a better number. The imaging beat prioritises CT because he is transportable now and may not stay so, and states plainly that the scan has not resulted. Worked example 0.1.0 drives the ordinary controls through the real engine to the handoff and asks the tutor for its narration rather than storing a copy. A test asserts that no beat anywhere gives an antithrombotic, names a rate-control drug or dose, reads the CT, or states the diagnosis. tests/unit/acute-aortic-syndrome-worked-example.test.ts verifies every beat and every refusal against the real engine, and tests/ui/emergency-acute-aortic-syndrome.test.tsx verifies the tray, silence when unassisted, stable controls while watching, and version binding.

src/modules/anesthesia/ui/Debrief.tsx maps the declared objectives to accepted engine events; the no-action path meets none and the expert path meets all five. The counterfactual is the one a symmetric first examination invites: the common-error path reviews the initial pattern and escalates on the strength of the story alone, without repeating the pulses that turn a suspicion into three disagreeing territories, and is refused because the engine gates it. The recovery path reaches for the repeat examination before the initial pattern has been reviewed and is refused, reaches for the imaging priority before the anti-impulse intent it travels with and is refused again, and still completes from the same positions.
